clue.text: I find smoker unusually annoying

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something done unusually is not done in its normal order, so the following word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A non-smoker grumbles that a fellow smoker is getting on their nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irksome irritates or bothers you, a straightforward synonym for annoying.

clue.text: Stumble upon hit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to meet or find by chance
second meaning: to crash into something, as a car might a wall

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like one action, tripping over a blow, but it is two separate meanings of the same phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both meeting someone by chance and colliding physically with an obstacle.

clue.text: Authority stays tight-lipped?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the power to decide or approve, as in 'on whose word?'
second, punning meaning: someone keeping quiet says nothing, and O is nothing

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as SAYS O: O is the crossword's usual nothing, so it means 'says nothing', which is staying tight-lipped. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the final word or official permission on a matter is a person's say-so, their power of approval.

clue.text: Aware of company boss trapped at home with dreadful flu

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so one piece sits enclosed within the other

parts.note: MD is managing director, the head of a company
someone at home is in

indicators.note: dreadful suggests a mess, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A sick executive stuck at home with flu stays conscious of the company.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has the boss trapped at home, but the wordplay works the other way round: the company boss does the trapping.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mindful of something is to keep it in your thoughts, being conscious or heedful of it.

clue.text: Iodine or mercury initially found in fish used as organic fuel

indicators.note: things found in something are inside it, so these letters sit within another word

parts.note: a bass is a fish, here split around the inserted letters

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding three words

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A chemistry warning that poisonous elements in fish end up in material burned for energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Iodine and mercury tempt you towards chemical symbols I and HG, but only the first letters of the three words are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant and animal matter burned to produce energy is known collectively as biomass.

clue.text: One after another reported trainee

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so we want a spelling that sounds like the phrase

parts.note: things done one after another happen in turn

explanation.surface: Trainees arrive one by one, according to the gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: An intern is a student or junior taking on work to gain experience, a kind of trainee.

clue.text: High spirits as police impound posh car — mine's broken down!

indicators.note: to impound is to seize and lock away, so the police word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
RR is Rolls-Royce, the classic posh car

indicators.note: something broken down is in pieces, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Laughter erupts as police tow away a broken-down Rolls, its owner protesting.
explanation.definitionFit: Merriment is cheerful fun and laughter, the same as being in high spirits.

clue.text: Woman in front of redhead is heavenly!

indicators.note: in front of places one piece before the other in a down answer

parts.note: Stella is a woman's name

indicators.note: a head is at the top, so only the opening letter of the word it is attached to is kept

parts.note: the head of red is its first letter

explanation.surface: An admirer declares the woman standing before a red-haired one to be divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' looks like one word for a ginger person, but it splits as red plus its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar means relating to the stars, so of the heavens, celestial.

clue.text: Praying to find unusually gifted child

indicators.note: unusually tells us the preceding letters are not in their usual order and must be rearranged

parts.note: all thirteen letters of these three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Parents pray that their offspring will turn out remarkably talented.
explanation.definitionFit: A child prodigy, a youngster with exceptional talent far beyond their years, is an unusually gifted child.

clue.text: Within reason, lying can be just

indicators.note: within says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A moral musing that telling lies may sometimes be justified, within limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like fair or justified, matching the moral surface, but here it is the adverb meaning merely.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, only means merely or no more than, the same as just in 'just a minute'.

clue.text: Having no direction for course makes one bound to fail

parts.note: taken as written
N is north, a compass direction
a starter is the first course of a meal

explanation.surface: A runner with no sense of direction on the course is sure to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a racetrack, but it is a course at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or person with no chance of succeeding is called a nonstarter in everyday speech.

clue.text: Unique, if intermittent, about English

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: something intermittent is on-off, working only some of the time
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Something is described as special, though only occasionally so, regarding the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if intermittent' reads as a hedge on 'Unique'; the 'if' is only a link, and intermittent is the hyphenated adjective on-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off happens or is made only once, so it is unique, with nothing like it.

clue.text: Skipping page two, pick up from where things take off

indicators.note: skipping means leaving out, so the paper's letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: two of anything make a pair
P is the abbreviation for page, the letter to be removed
to field a ball in cricket or baseball is to pick it up

explanation.surface: Instructions for a reader: jump past page two and resume from where events begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'page two' reads as one phrase, a page number, but the two words do different jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: An airfield is a stretch of ground where aircraft depart and land, a place planes leave the ground.

clue.text: Routine to Marilyn, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible version among others, so the letters before it may be arranged differently

parts.note: all nine letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A daily routine as it might have looked to Marilyn Monroe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' looks like it is hedging the guess about Marilyn, but it is the anagram signal; fittingly, Marilyn Monroe was born Norma Jeane.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual, everyday state of affairs, the ordinary pattern of life, is normality or routine.

clue.text: Doctored alumni pic belonging to the council

indicators.note: a doctored item has been tampered with, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: all nine letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A faked photograph of former students is owned by the local authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Municipal describes things run by or relating to a town or city's local government.

clue.text: Careful to keep in the final beat

indicators.note: to keep something in is to hold it inside, so one word encloses the letter

parts.note: wary means cautious

indicators.note: final picks out just the last letter of the next word

parts.note: the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: Musical advice to take care to hold the last beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like a noun about rhythm, but it is the adjective meaning worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beat, in informal usage, means exhausted, which is what weary means.

clue.text: Express a view nothing is next to wood

indicators.note: next to sets one piece directly beside the other

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
pine is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: Someone says nothing beats a spot beside the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, giving your thoughts on a matter.

clue.text: Make a show, when freshening up decor

indicators.note: freshening something gives it a new look, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: all seven letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Redecorating a home becomes a performance in itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freshening up' reads as one phrase, but only 'freshening' is the signal; 'up' joins the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To produce a play or film is to stage or create it, so it means putting on a show.

clue.text: Disturbing sermon with bit concerning one of hell's torments

indicators.note: disturbing things moves them out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, the rest of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A frightening preacher includes a passage on the punishments of the damned.
explanation.walkthrough: Brimstone is an old word for sulphur; fire and brimstone are the traditional torments of hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning sulphur, as in hellfire and brimstone, is one of the punishments of the damned in scripture.

clue.text: Tar of wreck penetrated by saltwater, not initially

indicators.note: something penetrated has another thing pushed inside it

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or wreck

indicators.note: not initially tells us to remove the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: brine is salt water, here losing its first letter

explanation.surface: A shipwreck holed by seawater, with tar as the substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' looks like the black sticky substance, but it is old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tar, from tarpaulin, is a traditional nickname for a sailor, and a mariner is a seaman.

clue.text: Kind of family with funny uncle caught abandoning car

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so one letter is dropped from the vehicle

parts.note: taken as written
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught, removed here

explanation.surface: A family with an eccentric uncle who was arrested after leaving his car.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear family is the household unit of two parents and their children, one type of family.

clue.text: Hang out under crafts' centre making woollen blanket

indicators.note: under in a down answer places the rearranged piece below the other
centre keeps only the middle letters of the word it follows

parts.note: the two middle letters of this six-letter word

indicators.note: out suggests the word is put out of order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Knitters hang their work in the craft centre to produce a woolly throw.
explanation.definitionFit: An afghan is a knitted or crocheted woollen blanket or throw, often made of squares.

clue.text: Made to take in army agent?

parts.note: an army is a military force
a fed is an American federal agent, an FBI officer

explanation.surface: A question whether an army spy was tricked or recruited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take in' suggests deceive, but here it means swallow food.
explanation.definitionFit: Being force-fed means being compelled to eat or swallow, made to take food in.

clue.text: Second jeer erupting on court

indicators.note: on here means followed by, setting the court piece after the first
erupting suggests bursting apart, so the letters of the taunt are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A tennis scene: a second round of booing breaks out on court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a time unit or an ordinal, but it is the noun for imperfect goods sold cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: Factory seconds are flawed items not up to standard, the same as rejects.

clue.text: Drink nearly the entire carafe with a sorbet

indicators.note: nearly the entire means everything except a little, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a carafe is a jug for wine or water
a sorbet is an ice, a frozen dessert

explanation.surface: Someone downs almost a whole carafe of wine alongside dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Juice is a drink pressed from fruit, served on its own or with a meal.

clue.text: Attack the piece and get an unfair advantage

parts.note: to jump someone is to attack them suddenly
taken as written
piece is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A chess or board-game tactic: capture the piece and gain the edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' suggests a chessman, but it is gangster slang for a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: To jump the gun is to start before the signal, like a sprinter leaving early, gaining an unfair head start.

clue.text: Couple featured in Time Out

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: Time Out is a London listings magazine, so the two words look like one title.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people in a romantic relationship are informally called an item, meaning a couple.

clue.text: Quickest route to get worker in front of queue

parts.note: a worker bee, the crossword's standard worker

explanation.definitionFit: A beeline is the straightest, most direct path somewhere, like a bee flying back to its hive.

clue.text: Amount owed by retired artist rises

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word is read backwards
